entry.title: [NEW] MAL-2026-17372: Malicious code in @ostyado/baileys (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in @ostyado/baileys (npm)

Aliases: GHSA-v73c-2rgc-m2jx

Affected:

  • @ostyado/baileys

This package is part of a large family (100+ identified as of September 2026) of near-identical forks of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that inject a covert channel-subscription action into the WhatsApp socket layer. On connect, the injected code issues an authenticated `w:mex` FOLLOW query (query_id 7871414976211147) against one or more attacker-chosen WhatsApp Channel/Newsletter JIDs, using the installer's own authenticated WhatsApp session -- silently subscribing the victim's account to channels it never asked to join. The target JID(s) are hidden from casual source review via one of several obfuscation techniques observed across the family: a plain string literal, base64 encoding, base64+XOR, or a char-code array reconstructed at runtime. Some variants instead fetch a mutable, attac…

entry.content:
Malicious code in @apexacc/cli (npm)

  • @apexacc/cli

@apexacc/cli is distributed by "Apex Accelerator" (Apex Arena), a fake Web3 accelerator that lures crypto founders with free AI credits and audits. entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17923: Malicious code in @apexacc/audit (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in @apexacc/audit (npm)

Affected:

  • @apexacc/audit

@apexacc/audit is the companion package to @apexacc/cli in the "Apex Accelerator" campaign (Elastic Security Labs REF8801, 2026-10-12). It exposes an MCP server with 18 "security tools" that all return fabricated output (for example a fixed Slither report and a "NOT A HONEYPOT" verdict), registers itself in Claude Desktop, Cursor and Windsurf MCP configs, and on Windows requests elevation to add a Defender exclusion for its folder and attempts to disable Smart App Control. It carries the same verification bootstrap as @apexacc/cli (macOS CloudSyncD dropper; Windows staged infostealer). The package returns "Not found" from the npm registry as of 2026-10-15, but installed copies persist. All versions affected. Indicators from Elastic's report.

References:

  • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/threat-command/apex-accelerator-malicious-npm-packages

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc: lodash vulnerable to Code Injection via `_.template` imports key names
entry.content:
lodash vulnerable to Code Injection via `_.template` imports key names

Aliases: CVE-2026-4800

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • lodash — fixed in 4.18.0
  • lodash-es — fixed in 4.18.0
  • lodash-amd — fixed in 4.18.0
  • lodash.template — fixed in 4.18.0

### Impact The fix for [CVE-2021-23337](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm) added validation for the `variable` option in `_.template` but did not apply the same validation to `options.imports` key names. Both paths flow into the same `Function()` constructor sink. When an application passes untrusted input as `options.imports` key names, an attacker can inject default-parameter expressions that execute arbitrary code at template compilation time. Additionally, `_.template` uses `assignInWith` to merge imports, which enumerates inherited properties via `for..in`. If `Object.prototype` has been polluted by any other vector, the polluted keys are copied into the imports object and passed to `Function()`. ### Patches Users should upgrade to version 4.18.0. The fix applies…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh: lodash vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via array path bypass in `_.unset` and `_.omit`
entry.content:
lodash vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via array path bypass in `_.unset` and `_.omit`

Aliases: CVE-2026-2950

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L

Affected:

  • lodash — fixed in 4.18.0
  • lodash-es — fixed in 4.18.0
  • lodash-amd — fixed in 4.18.0
  • lodash.unset — fixed in 4.18.0

### Impact Lodash versions 4.17.23 and earlier are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. The fix for [CVE-2025-13465](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg) only guards against string key members, so an attacker can bypass the check by passing array-wrapped path segments. This allows deletion of properties from built-in prototypes such as `Object.prototype`, `Number.prototype`, and `String.prototype`. The issue permits deletion of prototype properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior. ### Patches This issue is patched in 4.18.0. ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to the patched version.

References:

  • https://github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh
  • https://github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-2950

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg: Lodash has Prototype Pollution Vulnerability in `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions
entry.content:
Lodash has Prototype Pollution Vulnerability in `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions

Aliases: CVE-2025-13465

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/E:P

Affected:

  • lodash — fixed in 4.17.23
  • lodash.unset
  • lodash-es — fixed in 4.17.23
  • lodash-amd — fixed in 4.17.23

### Impact Lodash versions 4.0.0 through 4.17.22 are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. An attacker can pass crafted paths which cause Lodash to delete methods from global prototypes. The issue permits deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior. ### Patches This issue is patched on 4.17.23.
